<u>**7-B.**</u>  Whereas Section <u>**2(14)**</u> provides the definition of “<u>**order**</u>” in the following manner:- 

“(14) “order” means the formal expression of any decision of a Civil Court which is not a decree:” 

<u>**7-C**</u>.  The joint analysis of the above noted provisions clearly indicates that a decree is the formal expression of an adjudication by the court by virtue of which it conclusively determines the rights of the parties with regard to all or any of the matters in controversy in the suit which may either be a preliminary decree or final decree whereas order contemplates the formal expression of any decision of a Civil Court which does not qualify to be a decree. It is well recognized principle of law that decree always follows a judgment and the judgment is the statement given by the judge of the grounds of a decree or order. 

<u>**7-D**</u>.  From the above noted provisions of CPC, order for cancellation of bail cannot be termed to be a “decree” which could have been executed. Hence, in this sequel, the petitioner cannot be said to be “judgment-debtor” and respondent No.2 cannot be termed as “decree-holder”.
